jobs.title: Business Systems Analyst
jobs.description:
Inside the Role

This is an exciting opportunity to join a global company and industry leader. Daimler Truck Financial Services (DTFS) North America headquarters is near the Ballantyne Bowl, in Charlotte, NC. We are proud to be able to offer stable employment, excellent compensation, benefits, and tremendous career growth opportunities.

The ideal candidate will possess a can-do attitude with a combination of technical aptitude, business acumen, analytical thinking, and a passion for continuous improvement. Successful candidates are curious, self-motivated problem solvers who can effectively balance day-to-day operational support with long-term strategic initiatives.

Posting Information

We provide a scheduled posting end date to assist our candidates with their application planning. While this date reflects our latest plans, it is subject to change, and postings may be extended or removed earlier than expected.

We Take Care of Our Team

Position offers a starting salary range of $83,125 – $100,625 USD

Pay Offered Dependent On Knowledge, Skills, And Experience.

Benefits include annual bonus program; 401k company contribution with company match up to 6% as well as non-elective company contribution of 3 - 7% depending on age; starting at 4 weeks paid vacation; 13+ calendar holidays; 8 weeks paid parental leave; employee assistance program; comprehensive healthcare plans and wellness programs; onsite fitness (at some locations); tuition assistance and volunteer paid time off; short-term and long-term disability plans.

What You Drive At DTFS

DTFS is the Captive finance partner for Daimler Truck, the largest commercial truck manufacturer in the world based on production volume. Freightliner, Western Star, and Thomas Built Bus are Daimler’s most widely recognized truck brands in North America. DTFS $15B+ North America loan portfolio is spread out across several major customer segments, including truck fleets, truck dealerships, and independent truck owner operators.

Within DTFS, the Business Solutions Group (BSG) is responsible for the performance of our critical business systems. The BSG leads and supports the requirements gathering, design, implementation, maintenance, and continuous improvement of DTFS business systems. Altogether, the BSG supports a total of 40k users across 22 systems within North America.

A Business Systems Analyst needs to have a very well-rounded skill set. On average, your time will typically be split, where 20%-40% goes toward supporting day-to-day operations, maintenance efforts, and resolving user requests in accordance with our SLAs. The remaining 60%-80% of your time will be invested in identifying improvement opportunities, and quantifying those so they can be prioritized, planned, implemented, and validated.

Within the Business Solutions Group, our team supports two systems, Salesforce and Five9.

About Salesforce: Salesforce is a cloud-based customer relationship management (CRM) platform used to centralize customer, account, contact, opportunity, case, activity, and interaction data in one system. Organizations commonly use Salesforce to support sales, customer service, marketing, operations, reporting, workflow automation, and customer engagement. For DTFS, Salesforce helps business teams manage customer relationships, track work, improve visibility into operational activity, and create a more consistent user and customer experience across the organization.
About Five9: Five9 is a cloud-based contact center platform used to manage customer interactions across voice and digital channels. Organizations commonly use Five9 to support inbound and outbound calling, call routing, interactive voice response (IVR), intelligent virtual agents (IVA), agent desktop tools, quality monitoring, reporting, and operational performance management. For DTFS, Five9 helps customer-facing teams handle high-volume service interactions more efficiently, improve visibility into call activity and service performance, and support consistent, responsive customer experiences.

Knowledge You Should Bring

BS/BA Business Administration, Computer Information Systems (CIS), or Information Technology and prefer 2-4 years of relevant experience.
Familiarity with enterprise business applications, including CRM, contact center, workflow, reporting, or other operational systems.
Ambitious, curious, reliable, and coachable, with a demonstrated ability to learn new technologies, business processes, and industry concepts quickly.
A team player who takes initiative, takes pride in their work, and can work effectively both independently and collaboratively in a cross-functional team environment.
Well-organized, structured, flexible, and adaptable, with the ability to effectively prioritize and manage multiple initiatives, projects, and support requests.
Active listener. Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to engage stakeholders across multiple levels of the organization.
Experience or familiarity with gathering business requirements and translating them into system solutions that improve operational efficiency, user experience, and business outcomes.
Demonstrated ability to investigate, troubleshoot, identify root causes, and resolve system, process, and data-related issues while maintaining a high level of customer service.
Experience documenting business processes, requirements, functional specifications, workflows, and system configurations.
Familiarity with system implementations, enhancements, testing activities, user acceptance testing (UAT), and production deployments.
Understanding of data management principles, reporting concepts, and how system changes impact business processes.
Microsoft 365 High Proficiency

Exceptional Candidates Might Have

Lean Six Sigma Certifications
Salesforce Certifications
Five9 Certifications
System implementation experience
Experience supporting Salesforce, including user administration, security, reporting, dashboards, workflow automation, or platform configuration.
Experience supporting Five9 or other cloud-based contact center platforms, including IVA/IVR.
Understanding of customer service, call center, collections, loan servicing, finance, or related operational business processes.
Experience with system integrations, APIs, data exchange processes, or middleware platforms.
Familiarity with Agile, Scrum, Lean, or continuous improvement methodologies.
Salesforce Administrator Certification and/or other relevant platform certifications.
Experience creating and delivering end-user training, knowledge articles, and system documentation.

Where We Work

This position is open to applicants who can work in (or relocate to) the following location(s)-

Charlotte, NC US. Relocation assistance is not available for this position.

Schedule Type:

Hybrid (4 days per week in-office / 1 day remote). This schedule builds our #OneTeamBestTeam culture, provides an unparalleled customer experience, and creates innovative solutions through in-person collaboration.

Daimler Truck Financial is the captive financial services provider for the Daimler Trucks North America family of commercial vehicle products, including Freightliner Trucks, Western Star, SelecTrucks, Sprinter Vans, Thomas Built Buses and Fuso. We have specialized in financing commercial vehicles for more than 40 years. This proven experience gives us critical insights into helping businesses overcome challenges unique to the trucking industry. Additionally, we offer a range of financing solutions that can be customized to meet each individual business's needs, from owner-operators to large fleet managers and nearly every venture in-between.

To achieve our goal of being the first-choice provider of vehicle financial products and services that support our brands, dealers and customers, we are looking for talented, diverse and inspired people with the skills, experience and innovative spirit to provide a first-class experience at every turn. We are committed to providing a great workplace environment that fosters a culture of openness, support and camaraderie. Our employee programs and benefits are reflective of our values and are designed to promote growth, balance and wellness in many aspects of your career and life.

Partner Forces is a management consulting firm helping homeland security organizations solve some of their most pressing and complex challenges. We partner with government agencies and industry to strengthen national security and critical infrastructure through expertise in strategy, program management, stakeholder engagement, technology implementation, preparedness, and business transformation.

As a growing firm, every employee has the opportunity to contribute not only to our clients' success, but also to the future of Partner Forces. Partner Forces is looking for a hands-on Data Engineer to support a federal cybersecurity client at the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). We're looking for someone who enjoys solving complex data problems, connecting systems, and finding smarter ways to automate processes. In this role, you'll help bring together data from different sources, build and improve data pipelines, and develop automated solutions that make data more accessible, reliable, and useful. The ideal candidate is a strong technical problem solver who thinks automation-first, is comfortable working with messy or disconnected datasets, and enjoys figuring out how to make systems work better together.

Design, build, and maintain data pipelines that integrate information from multiple systems and sources.
Develop automated processes to collect, transform, organize, and move data efficiently.
Integrate structured and unstructured datasets to improve data accessibility and usability.
Use SQL, Python, and other tools to clean, transform, and manage data.
Identify opportunities to replace manual processes with scalable, automated solutions.
Troubleshoot data integration challenges and improve data quality, consistency, and reliability.
Support data platforms, databases, and cloud-based environments.

Collaborate with technical teams and mission stakeholders to understand needs and develop practical solutions.
Support data that enables cybersecurity operations, analytics, reporting, and other mission capabilities.

Must be a U.S. Citizen with an active Top Secret security clearance.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent relevant experience.

Hands-on experience building data pipelines and ETL/ELT processes.

Experience with metadata management, data catalogs, or data governance.

Experience with APIs, workflow automation, or modern data integration tools.

If your application looks like a match, someone from our People Operations team will reach out to schedule a phone screening. jobs.title: Consultant, Data Engineer - Reference Data Management
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about being part of a team at a Fortune 100 company with nearly $70 billion in annual sales that delivers extraordinary care to help individuals and businesses prepare for and protect their future? If so, then Nationwide Financial could be the place for you! At Nationwide®, “on your side” goes beyond just words. Our customers and partners are at the center of everything we do and we’re looking for associates who are passionate about delivering extraordinary care.

This role is an individual contributor with a hybrid work expectation (2 days per week in the office). It is our intention to fill this role in Columbus, Ohio or Scottsdale, Arizona, however, on occasion, applications from internal candidates that are working remotely who bring critical industry skills and relevant experience may be considered.

Why this role matters

Product and fund data supports important business processes across Nationwide. In this role, you’ll help develop a governed reference data capability that makes this information easier for teams and systems to use consistently. You’ll help establish trusted data definitions, clear stewardship practices, and reliable ways to share updates across the organization.

You’ll also contribute to Nationwide’s broader enterprise data strategy by helping extend this capability to additional data domains. Your work will support high-quality, traceable data and help teams deliver dependable insights and services.

The opportunity

Embedded within Nationwide Financial’s business organization, this is a hands-on technical role focused on configuring, integrating, and operating the Semarchy reference data management platform. You’ll work close to the business while serving as the technical practitioner who turns business requirements into platform models, workflows, data loads, integrations, and maintained views and APIs. Semarchy is designed to be configured around business data and stewardship needs; you’ll ensure the resulting data is reliable, secure, and easy to use. Direct Semarchy experience is valuable, alongside practical data engineering and governance skills.

You’ll work with business data owners and stewards, who define the meaning of each data set, identify authoritative sources, and make business decisions about what is correct. You’ll configure and support the solution based on those decisions, including business rules and access controls, and stay engaged as data changes and issues arise. Business ownership stays with the domain; your contribution is the technical implementation and operation of the capability.

What You’ll Do

Semarchy Consultant

Partner with business data owners and stewards to understand reference data needs, then translate their decisions into Semarchy models—for example, product and fund entities, attributes, relationships, and hierarchies.
Configure validation and match/merge rules, along with authoring and approval workflows, so updates follow agreed business rules and stewardship practices.
Recommend practical role and access patterns for people who create, review, and approve data; support new domains and users as they adopt the platform.

Semarchy Data Engineer

Build and operate data loads and integrations that bring product and fund reference data from source systems into Semarchy and deliver approved data to Snowflake, the primary consumption path for most downstream applications, while supporting other required integrations.
Maintain views and APIs that provide governed access where needed, without coupling consumers to the platform’s internal tables—for example, supporting an application that retrieves current, approved fund codes.
Monitor pipelines, investigate failures, and reconcile records across sources, Semarchy, and destinations; add checks for accuracy, completeness, and timeliness.
Break requirements into technical work, estimate delivery, and apply secure engineering practices as data flows and integrations are built and maintained.

Data Governance Advisor

Work with data owners and stewards to document definitions and identify critical data elements—for example, clarifying what a product or fund code represents and the rules it must meet.
Support quality profiling, lineage, metadata, and documentation so users can understand where reference data comes from, what it means, and how it should be used.

jobs.description:
About Us

At LangChain, our mission is to make intelligent agents ubiquitous. We build the foundation for agent engineering in the real world, helping developers move from prototypes to production-ready AI agents that teams can rely on. We began as widely adopted open-source tools and have grown to also offer a platform for building, evaluating, deploying, and operating agents at scale.

LangChain is a place where your contributions can shape how this technology shows up in the real world.

Today, our platform includes LangSmith (Observability, Evaluation, Deployment, Fleet, and Sandboxes), our open source frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, and Deep Agents), and the newly launched LangSmith Engine for autonomous agent improvement. We have 100M+ monthly open source downloads, 6,000+ active LangSmith customers, and 5 of the Fortune 10 use LangSmith in production (+ 35% of the Fortune 500 overall), including teams at Klarna, Clay, Coinbase, Workday, Lyft, Cloudflare, Harvey, Rippling, Vanta, LinkedIn, Monday.com, Nvidia, and Bridgewater.

About the Team:

You'll join our GTM Systems team, which owns the systems LangChain's go-to-market actually runs on — Salesforce above all: the account and contact model, territory and routing, the sales process from first touch to closed-won, and the quote-to-cash and provisioning stack behind it.

We design and ship internal product for the GTM organization. AI agents do a growing share of the building: they draft design docs, open changes, and run Salesforce deployments, while humans hold the approval gates. Build capacity — engineers plus the agent bench — sits on this team, and you'll help decide what it works on next.

About the Role:

You'll own the requirements, prioritization, and quality bar for LangChain's Salesforce-centered GTM systems, turning ambiguous revenue-team needs into shipped process and systems changes that scale.

This is not a ticket queue role. You'll be accountable for a small number of high-leverage GTM systems programs at a time: defining the problem, aligning stakeholders, specifying the solution, and ensuring what ships changes how the revenue org operates.

You'll work across Sales, Marketing, Partnerships, Support, and Finance in a fast-changing environment where priorities move quickly and influence matters more than reporting lines. The core challenge is operating with authority but not control: aligning teams around tradeoffs as the business changes underneath the plan.

You won't be expected to write production code. You will be expected to write clear enough specifications that engineers and AI coding agents can build from them, and to review the output with enough Salesforce and systems judgment to decide whether it is correct.

Location:
San Francisco Bay Area — in office 4 days a week. The people whose processes you're redesigning are in this building, and so are the engineers who build LangGraph.

What You'll Own:

Carry multi-quarter programs

Own the Salesforce sales process from lead to close — routing, qualification, territory assignment, and stage progression — driving each initiative from discovery through UAT, change management, and adoption.
Be the person stakeholders come to before they file a request, especially when the system was never designed for what the business now needs.
Own the intake and prioritization model for hundreds of quarterly GTM systems requests, ensuring the team works on the highest-leverage business problems rather than the loudest tickets.

Own What Gets Specified And What Ships

Run discovery and turn ambiguous asks into BRDs, process flows, data models, and acceptance criteria — with a clear problem statement and ROI justification, precise enough to execute without a second conversation.
Hold the quality gate: you write the specification, engineers and coding agents write the code, and nothing reaches production without your sign-off.
Run vendor evaluations when the right answer is buy, integrate, or replace rather than build.

Protect revenue data integrity

Trace anomalies in revenue fields — Net ARR, initial pipeline, lead source — back to the automation, trigger, or integration that wrote them.
Own the reconciliation seam between Salesforce, usage-based billing, and cloud-marketplace transactions.
Identify which design decisions are load-bearing and which are cosmetic, and catch the downstream failure modes before they reach production.

What Success Looks Like:

In your first 6–12 months, you might:

Redesign the lead-to-opportunity process so routing, qualification, and stage progression are measurable, enforceable, and adopted by the field.
Create a prioritization model for hundreds of GTM systems requests per quarter, with clear tradeoffs and business rationale.
Ship a Salesforce change that improves pipeline hygiene, quote-to-cash accuracy, provisioning reliability, or cloud marketplace reconciliation.
Establish a specification and UAT standard that engineers and AI agents can reliably build against.
Build enough trust with Sales, Marketing, Partnerships, Support, and Finance that stakeholders bring you the problem before they prescribe the solution.

What You'll Need to Be Successful:

Systems and domain depth

Domain and tenure — 6–8 years in business systems, sales systems, revenue systems, or GTM systems, with Salesforce as your primary platform throughout.
Sales process depth — you've partnered with Sales Ops on the things reps feel every day: territory and account coverage, lead qualification and routing, stage gates, and pipeline and forecast hygiene.
Sales systems / RevOps depth — experience across quote-to-cash, CPQ, territory and lead routing, forecasting, or adjacent revenue processes.
Technical fluency — you can read a data model, a Flow, and enough Apex to design against what's really there, even though you are not expected to write production code.

Program leadership

Program ownership — you've been the single accountable owner, at the working level negotiating the commitments yourself, of a program that spanned four or more functions and changed how a revenue org works day to day.
Release risk — you've delivered a program into a core system on a release process you didn't control, where another team's change could break your release.
Re-scoping under change — you've re-scoped a program mid-flight because the business changed under it, a sponsor moved, or the original scope no longer matched reality.
Holding the line — you've turned down a request with executive backing and kept the relationship; you hold the line when something breaks pricing discipline, a legal constraint, or the architecture, and you arrive with the alternative.

Judgment and communication

One tradeoff, two audiences — you write for the reader in front of you, not the one you find easiest: the VP gets the page, the engineer gets the spec.
Maximum agency — you find the friction and start the project. You don't wait for a ticket.
AI judgment — you give an agent the same brief you'd give a new engineer, and you check its work the same way.
Architecture judgment — you know which design calls are load-bearing and which are cosmetic: why a usage event belongs on its own object rather than a field on Account, and how you'd catch that renaming one picklist breaks the provisioning saga before anyone deploys it.

Strong Signals:

None of these is a screen; any one makes you useful faster.

You've owned a core Salesforce object domain — Account, Contact, Lead, or Opportunity — through a full redesign.
You've traced a Salesforce field into a usage record into a provisioning step, and seen what broke downstream when it moved.
You've worked with cloud marketplace operations — AWS or GCP private offers, co-sell, entitlement mapping, metering, and the failure modes when they break.
You've worked with usage-based billing systems such as Metronome, Orb, or similar, and CRM↔billing identity reconciliation.
You have LangChain or LangGraph experience, or you're excited to learn it here from the people who build it.

Annual salary range: $180-200k USD

Compensation Philosophy:

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks.

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.

Troubleshoot data integration challenges and improve data quality, consistency, and reliability.
Support data platforms, databases, and cloud-based environments.

Collaborate with technical teams and mission stakeholders to understand needs and develop practical solutions.
Support data that enables cybersecurity operations, analytics, reporting, and other mission capabilities.

Bachelor's degree or equivalent relevant experience.
Approximately 3–7 years of experience in data engineering, data integration, automation, or a related technical field.
Hands-on experience building data pipelines and ETL/ELT processes.
Strong SQL skills and experience working with databases and multiple data sources.
Experience using Python or similar scripting languages to automate data processes.
Experience integrating, transforming, and managing complex datasets.
Familiarity with cloud environments such as AWS, Azure, or GCP.
Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
Ability to collaborate with technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
Candidates must be local to the DMV area and available to work onsite 2–3 days per week. This is a required in-person commitment.

Experience with metadata management, data catalogs, or data governance.
Experience supporting federal cybersecurity or DHS missions.
Experience with APIs, workflow automation, or modern data integration tools.
Familiarity with data warehousing, data lakes, or modern data platforms.

If your application looks like a match, someone from our People Operations team will reach out to schedule a phone screening. About Us

At LangChain, our mission is to make intelligent agents ubiquitous. We build the foundation for agent engineering in the real world, helping developers move from prototypes to production-ready AI agents that teams can rely on. We began as widely adopted open-source tools and have grown to also offer a platform for building, evaluating, deploying, and operating agents at scale.

With $125M raised at Series B from IVP, Sequoia, Benchmark, CapitalG, and Sapphire Ventures, we’re at a stage where we’re continuing to develop new products, growth is accelerating, and all team members have meaningful impact on what we build and how we work together. LangChain is a place where your contributions can shape how this technology shows up in the real world.

Today, our platform includes LangSmith (Observability, Evaluation, Deployment, Fleet, and Sandboxes), our open source frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, and Deep Agents), and the newly launched LangSmith Engine for autonomous agent improvement. We have 100M+ monthly open source downloads, 6,000+ active LangSmith customers, and 5 of the Fortune 10 use LangSmith in production (+ 35% of the Fortune 500 overall), including teams at Klarna, Clay, Coinbase, Workday, Lyft, Cloudflare, Harvey, Rippling, Vanta, LinkedIn, Monday.com, Nvidia, and Bridgewater.

About the Team:

You'll join our GTM Systems team, which owns the systems LangChain's go-to-market actually runs on — Salesforce above all: the account and contact model, territory and routing, the sales process from first touch to closed-won, and the quote-to-cash and provisioning stack behind it.

We design and ship internal product for the GTM organization. AI agents do a growing share of the building: they draft design docs, open changes, and run Salesforce deployments, while humans hold the approval gates. Build capacity — engineers plus the agent bench — sits on this team, and you'll help decide what it works on next.

About the Role:

You'll own the requirements, prioritization, and quality bar for LangChain's Salesforce-centered GTM systems, turning ambiguous revenue-team needs into shipped process and systems changes that scale.

This is not a ticket queue role. You'll be accountable for a small number of high-leverage GTM systems programs at a time: defining the problem, aligning stakeholders, specifying the solution, and ensuring what ships changes how the revenue org operates.

You'll work across Sales, Marketing, Partnerships, Support, and Finance in a fast-changing environment where priorities move quickly and influence matters more than reporting lines. The core challenge is operating with authority but not control: aligning teams around tradeoffs as the business changes underneath the plan.

You won't be expected to write production code. You will be expected to write clear enough specifications that engineers and AI coding agents can build from them, and to review the output with enough Salesforce and systems judgment to decide whether it is correct.

Location:
San Francisco Bay Area — in office 4 days a week. The people whose processes you're redesigning are in this building, and so are the engineers who build LangGraph.

What You'll Own:

Carry multi-quarter programs

Own the Salesforce sales process from lead to close — routing, qualification, territory assignment, and stage progression — driving each initiative from discovery through UAT, change management, and adoption.
Be the person stakeholders come to before they file a request, especially when the system was never designed for what the business now needs.
Own the intake and prioritization model for hundreds of quarterly GTM systems requests, ensuring the team works on the highest-leverage business problems rather than the loudest tickets.

Own What Gets Specified And What Ships

Run discovery and turn ambiguous asks into BRDs, process flows, data models, and acceptance criteria — with a clear problem statement and ROI justification, precise enough to execute without a second conversation.
Hold the quality gate: you write the specification, engineers and coding agents write the code, and nothing reaches production without your sign-off.
Run vendor evaluations when the right answer is buy, integrate, or replace rather than build.

Protect revenue data integrity

Trace anomalies in revenue fields — Net ARR, initial pipeline, lead source — back to the automation, trigger, or integration that wrote them.
Own the reconciliation seam between Salesforce, usage-based billing, and cloud-marketplace transactions.
Identify which design decisions are load-bearing and which are cosmetic, and catch the downstream failure modes before they reach production.

What Success Looks Like:

In your first 6–12 months, you might:

Redesign the lead-to-opportunity process so routing, qualification, and stage progression are measurable, enforceable, and adopted by the field.
Create a prioritization model for hundreds of GTM systems requests per quarter, with clear tradeoffs and business rationale.
Ship a Salesforce change that improves pipeline hygiene, quote-to-cash accuracy, provisioning reliability, or cloud marketplace reconciliation.
Establish a specification and UAT standard that engineers and AI agents can reliably build against.
Build enough trust with Sales, Marketing, Partnerships, Support, and Finance that stakeholders bring you the problem before they prescribe the solution.

What You'll Need to Be Successful:

Systems and domain depth

Domain and tenure — 6–8 years in business systems, sales systems, revenue systems, or GTM systems, with Salesforce as your primary platform throughout.
Sales process depth — you've partnered with Sales Ops on the things reps feel every day: territory and account coverage, lead qualification and routing, stage gates, and pipeline and forecast hygiene.
Sales systems / RevOps depth — experience across quote-to-cash, CPQ, territory and lead routing, forecasting, or adjacent revenue processes.
Technical fluency — you can read a data model, a Flow, and enough Apex to design against what's really there, even though you are not expected to write production code.

Program leadership

Program ownership — you've been the single accountable owner, at the working level negotiating the commitments yourself, of a program that spanned four or more functions and changed how a revenue org works day to day.
Release risk — you've delivered a program into a core system on a release process you didn't control, where another team's change could break your release.
Re-scoping under change — you've re-scoped a program mid-flight because the business changed under it, a sponsor moved, or the original scope no longer matched reality.
Holding the line — you've turned down a request with executive backing and kept the relationship; you hold the line when something breaks pricing discipline, a legal constraint, or the architecture, and you arrive with the alternative.

Judgment and communication

One tradeoff, two audiences — you write for the reader in front of you, not the one you find easiest: the VP gets the page, the engineer gets the spec.
Maximum agency — you find the friction and start the project. You don't wait for a ticket.
AI judgment — you give an agent the same brief you'd give a new engineer, and you check its work the same way.
Architecture judgment — you know which design calls are load-bearing and which are cosmetic: why a usage event belongs on its own object rather than a field on Account, and how you'd catch that renaming one picklist breaks the provisioning saga before anyone deploys it.

Strong Signals:

None of these is a screen; any one makes you useful faster.

You've owned a core Salesforce object domain — Account, Contact, Lead, or Opportunity — through a full redesign.
You've traced a Salesforce field into a usage record into a provisioning step, and seen what broke downstream when it moved.
You've worked with cloud marketplace operations — AWS or GCP private offers, co-sell, entitlement mapping, metering, and the failure modes when they break.
You've worked with usage-based billing systems such as Metronome, Orb, or similar, and CRM↔billing identity reconciliation.
You have LangChain or LangGraph experience, or you're excited to learn it here from the people who build it.

Annual salary range: $180-200k USD

Compensation Philosophy:

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks.

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. The Manufacturing Automation Engineer is responsible for identifying, developing, and implementing automation solutions across Port Alpha's shipyard production processes — plate cutting and profiling, panel and sub-assembly fabrication, robotic welding, block assembly, blast and paint, outfitting, material handling, and test — to improve throughput, quality, repeatability, safety, and cost efficiency. This role serves as the primary technical owner for automation projects from concept through production launch, partnering closely with Design Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Operations, Quality, and Supply Chain teams.

The role sits within Shipyard Optimization (Robotics & Autonomous Build) and works hand in hand with Saronic's central automation and software teams so that Port Alpha's automation architecture, controls standards, and MES integration stay aligned with the company-wide approach while fitting the realities of large-structure steel shipbuilding.

The ideal candidate combines strong manufacturing process knowledge with automation expertise and plays a critical role in designing products and processes that are optimized for scalable automated production. Following implementation and production stabilization, ownership transitions to Port Alpha Manufacturing Engineering for sustaining support and continuous improvement.

Responsibilities

Automation Strategy & Process Development

Identify manufacturing operations and workflows suitable for automation based on safety, quality, throughput, ergonomic, and cost considerations.
Develop automation roadmaps and business cases to support production scaling objectives, feeding the Port Alpha Production Systems Roadmap.
Evaluate and recommend automation technologies including robotics, machine vision, PLC-controlled systems, automated assembly and welding equipment, material handling systems, and test automation.
Lead feasibility studies, cycle time analysis, and ROI assessments for proposed automation initiatives.

Cross-Functional Product & Process Design

Partner with Design Engineering during product development to ensure vessels and their structures are designed for manufacturability and automation (DFMA/DFA).
Provide design feedback on tolerances, joining methods, part presentation, fixturing, assembly sequence, and inspection requirements to enable robust automated manufacturing processes.
Collaborate with Manufacturing Engineering and Shipyard Optimization to define scalable production architectures and standardized automation strategies that fit the facility layout and flow.

Automation Project Ownership

Own automation projects from concept development through equipment commissioning and production launch.
Define equipment specifications, statement of work (SOW), acceptance criteria, and validation plans for integrators and vendors.
Manage automation suppliers and system integrators throughout design, build, FAT, SAT, installation, and startup activities.
Coordinate equipment integration with facility infrastructure, MES systems, quality systems, and production controls.
Develop and execute process validation plans, capability studies, and production readiness reviews.

Production Launch & Handoff

Support pilot builds, process debugging, and ramp-to-rate activities during production launch.
Establish documentation packages including work instructions, PM requirements, spare parts lists, control plans, and troubleshooting guides.
Train Manufacturing Engineering, Operations, and Asset Reliability & Facility Operations teams on system functionality and maintenance requirements.
Transition ownership of stable production systems to Manufacturing Engineering for sustaining support and continuous improvement activities.

Continuous Improvement & Technical Leadership

Drive improvements in OEE, yield, uptime, cycle time, and labor efficiency through automation initiatives.
Standardize automation design practices, controls architecture, and equipment specifications across production lines and with Saronic's other manufacturing sites.
Support root cause investigations and corrective actions related to automated systems during launch phases.
Stay current with emerging manufacturing automation technologies and industry best practices, including shipbuilding-specific automation.

Experience implementing automated manufacturing systems in high-volume, heavy fabrication, or advanced manufacturing environments.
